 Cameron Diaz is returning to her roots for an upcoming Netflix comedy. Following a lengthy break from acting, the Charlie's Angels star is back and better than ever for an action-packed comedy project that's poised for release just ahead of the Christmas holiday.

 Diaz got her start in humorous hits like The Mask , My Best Friend's Wedding, and There's Something About Mary, all of which helped establish her as a comedic powerhouse . Now, she is returning to her favored genre for Netflix's Bad Day , and early trailers for the release promise a hilarious romp worthy of the 54-year-old star.
 The film follows Diaz, a mom striving to show up for her daughter despite enduring a truly horrendous day. Snippets included in a two-minute trailer tease a wild ride that includes an accidental robbery, at least one police standoff, and plenty of collateral damage. At the core of it all is a charming story of a mom who just wants to be there for her kids.

 A wealth of comedic talent has been tapped to appear alongside Diaz in Bad Day. A number of sidesplitting legends are on the cast list, including Ed O'Neill of Modern Family , Mark Duplass of The Morning Show , Ben Schwartz of Parks and Recreation , Rob Corddry of Hot Tub Time Machine , and frequent Saturday Night Live writer John Higgins. The release is directed by Jake Szymanski, who won a 2023 Peabody Award as an Entertainment Honoree for directing reality-hoax sitcom Jury Duty.

 Diaz took a lengthy break from acting following her 2014 appearance in Annie before returning in 2025 with another Netflix comedy. She and Jamie Foxx made a great pair in Back in Action , but the film failed to impress audiences. That's an unfortunate trend for Netflix, which has missed the mark with plenty of its recent comedic attempts. Bad Day might just be among the films that break that mold . Its top-tier cast, paired with a stellar writer in Laura Solon and an equally talented director, bodes well for the release. 
 The timing of Bad Day 's release also works in its favor. The film is set to arrive on Netflix right between the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, with an official release date of Dec. 11, 2026. That sets it up to be a staple of the 2026 holiday season.
